html:
The Wemba Wemba are an Aboriginal Australian people of northwestern Victoria and southwestern New South Wales, in the Mallee and Riverina country along the Murray. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

Their land is flat and dry away from the river, with lakes, swamps and red gum forest along the water. People fished and caught waterbirds on the river and lakes and gathered plant foods in the mallee. Neighbours on the map include the Wadi Wadi, the Baraba Baraba and the Yorta Yorta. Pastoral runs spread along the Murray from the 1840s. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
